item.title: What's next after a brutal stock plunge we might have seen coming
item.description: Stocks tanked this week as investors grew wary of tech investments that have seen years of growth. NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Katie Martin of the Financial Times about the global ripple effects.

item.title: Google employees protest AI in schools policy
item.description: More than 550 Google employees signed a petition to allow schools access to Search without AI. Parents and educators protested outside Google offices in 6 cities last week for the same ask.

item.title: Deadlocked again? U.N. climate talks in Turkey go into overtime
item.description: United Nations climate talks are heading into super overtime this weekend in Turkey. Negotiations were supposed to wrap up Friday but talks have spilled into a second night.

item.title: Inside a Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack release party in Miami
item.description: Music is a major part of the video game Grand Theft Auto. The latest release, Grand Theft Auto VI comes with its own carefully crafted soundtrack played on radio stations inside the game. The game is based in the fictional Vice City, based on Miami, Florida. WLRN's Alyssa Ramos went to a soundtrack release party to learn more about how the music of GTA VI captures Miami's vibe.

item.title: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village
item.description: In Southern Lebanon, the Army is taking over after Israeli forces withdraw. One grieving family returns to their village to find almost everything in their house destroyed.

item.title: NEA announces 2027 Jazz Masters class
item.description: The National Endowment for the Arts has named Terry Gibbs, Rufus Reid, Larry Ridley, Harvey Mason and John Edward Hasse as the newest musicians and advocates to receive the highest federal jazz honor.

item.title: Tech stocks end the week on a down note, despite Anthropic's mega-IPO
item.description: The stock market is ending the week down despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO and a strong Nvidia earnings report, largely thanks to investor jitters about the future of AI.
